open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries
open_points.question: Which metadata fields cross this boundary, how are file types such as symlinks and special files represented, and which fields may influence eligibility, source identity, preparation or the publication body?
options: Only a specified portable allowlist such as size, modification time and regular-file type is read; none is published
All filesystem stat metadata is available but only specified fields affect decisions
Platform-dependent metadata, extended attributes and link targets may also be consumed
open_points.default_guess: Read an explicit allowlist, require a regular file, treat every value as untrusted, and do not copy metadata into the publication body unless separately specified.

witness.initial: Two object folders contain identical file names and bytes but different modification times, permissions and extended attributes.
events: Syncthing-fork supplies both files and their metadata.
Calling flow asks what can be delivered.
outcomes: The deliverer ignores the differing metadata and reports identical eligibility and source identity.
The deliverer uses metadata in identity or eligibility and reports different source ids or statuses.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Actors and trust boundaries
open_points.text: file names, file metadata and bytes
open_points.question: Must the name, metadata and bytes describe one atomic version of a file, and what happens if Syncthing-fork replaces the file while they are being read?
options: Take or emulate a consistent snapshot and reject or retry when consistency cannot be established
Accept the bytes read even if the accompanying metadata came from another version
Bind only selected metadata such as size to the bytes and ignore changes to other fields
open_points.default_guess: Open one file handle, read metadata and bytes from that handle, verify relevant metadata again after reading, and reject or retry if a stable version cannot be established.

witness.initial: A chosen path initially contains version A.
events: Calling flow requests delivery of version A.
Syncthing-fork replaces the path with version B before the deliverer reads the bytes.
outcomes: The deliverer combines A's metadata with B's bytes and may place B.
The deliverer detects the version change and retries or refuses without placing either version.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions
open_points.text: each file with a status: ready, placed or published with its source id, or rejected with a reason
open_points.question: Does a rejected file also carry its source id, or is the source id present only for ready, placed and published files?
options: Every file, including a rejected file, carries a source id; rejection additionally carries a reason
Only ready, placed and published files carry a source id
Rejected files carry a source id only when identity could be established before rejection
open_points.default_guess: Return a source id for every file whose identity can be established, including rejected files, and define the field as absent when rejection prevents identity calculation.

witness.initial: A project contains one file whose format is not deliverable but whose path and bytes are readable.
events: Calling flow asks what can be delivered.
The deliverer classifies the file as rejected.
outcomes: The rejected entry contains both its source id and its reason.
The rejected entry contains its reason but no source id.

open_points.subject: 00_product.md:Primary actions
open_points.text: a photo that cannot be delivered is reported with its reason and no placement is made
open_points.question: What precisely counts as a placement, and which writes or durable side effects are permitted when delivery fails?
options: No write of any kind may survive the failed request
No prepared image or reference may survive, but internal audit, rejection or idempotency records may be written
An unreferenced prepared image may remain in the Portal store because only creation of its reference counts as placement
open_points.default_guess: Leave no prepared image or reference in the Portal store; permit only explicitly named internal records and clean up temporary files before returning the failure.

witness.initial: A chosen photo is readable but fails validation after preparation has begun.
events: Calling flow asks the deliverer to place the photo.
The deliverer writes prepared bytes and then encounters the validation failure.
The deliverer returns the failure reason.
outcomes: The prepared bytes and all durable request state are removed.
An orphan prepared image or durable failure record remains because no successful file reference was returned.
witness.observer: Client Portal or the owner on a later request
